Fig. 3. Qualitative results of ICL models on 3D segmentation tasks. For each 3D segmentation target, results are shown from two views. By utilizing green for correct overlaps (TP), red for false positive over-segmentations (FP), and blue for false negative misses (FN), this comparison plot visually highlights the overwhelming advantage of our model (on the far right), demonstrating the largest accurate green area with minimal red and blue errors compared to other baseline models.

Fig. 1. Overview of the UniMedSeg architecture. The model unifies diverse ICL contexts (including visual examples, interactive prompts, and language instructions) within a Transformer-Centric architecture. Specifically, when the context involves interactive prompts such as points or bounding boxes, the context image is the target image itself. Multimodal inputs are transformed into a unified one-dimensional token sequence and augmented with learnable Type Embeddings. Distinct RoPE strategies are applied. The global concatenate sequence then undergoes deep feature interaction via SplitEvaBlocks using a Decoupled Split Attention mechanism. Finally, target tokens are sliced and routed to dimension-specific decoders.
